text: Authentication is enforced at the API boundary. Business services accept a verified Principal and never parse bearer tokens directly.
Services use constructor injection. New dependencies must be represented by narrow protocols so unit tests can supply deterministic fakes.
Access tokens require issuer, audience, signature, expiry, and not-before validation. Failed validation returns a generic unauthorized response without disclosing which check failed.
Authentication establishes identity; authorization remains a separate deny-by-default policy check for each protected capability.
Security changes require tests for valid credentials, expired credentials, wrong audience, malformed input, missing credentials, and insufficient roles.
API integration tests assert status code, stable error shape, and that rejected requests never invoke the protected service.
Signing keys and credentials come from the deployment secret store. Configuration identifies key versions and supports overlap during rotation.
Record authentication outcome, reason category, issuer, and correlation ID. Never log raw access tokens, secrets, or unnecessary personal data.
Public API documentation describes the authentication scheme and error contract. The operator runbook covers key rotation and emergency revocation.
The design system uses an eight-pixel spacing grid and requires WCAG AA color contrast for interactive controls.
Nightly demand forecasts are partitioned by region and retained for thirteen months for seasonality analysis.
The mobile client resolves offline write conflicts with server timestamps and displays a non-blocking reconciliation notice.
Invoice totals use decimal arithmetic, preserve source currency, and apply tax only after line-level discounts.
Embedding releases require retrieval evaluation against the frozen relevance set and a drift report by language.
